summary: OIDC refresh tokens sometimes drop role claims after FIDO2 device-trust assertion, causing 403s on deployment-gateway
description:
Issue summary: Several internal engineers intermittently receive 403 Forbidden from deployment-gateway immediately after signing in with Okta OIDC + FIDO2 device-trust. Impact: blocks internal deploys and CI jobs for engineers using hardware-backed device trust. Background: This flow exchanges an Okta-issued ID token / refresh token and our auth service mints a session token with embedded RBAC claims. Symptoms started after a small change to the auth service's OIDC refresh handling and a recent Okta device-trust policy update.

Observed: users authenticate successfully at Okta, but subsequent requests to deployment-gateway return 403 with "missing_role" in gateway logs. Re-auth (full browser SSO) temporarily restores access.

Expected: device-trust assertion + refresh flow should preserve current RBAC claims (roles/groups) across refreshes.

Temporary impact workaround: instruct affected users to perform full SSO login (not relying on background refresh) or restart affected CI runners. We implemented a short-lived mitigation in auth-cache to aggressively evict session cache on 403s from gateway (see investigation_notes).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Enroll FIDO2 device and enable Okta Device Trust for user
2) Authenticate to Redwood Console via OIDC using device-trust (get id_token + refresh_token)
3) Let client perform background refresh to obtain a new session token via auth service
4) Immediately call deployment-gateway API endpoint used by CI or CLI (e.g., POST /deploys) and observe 403
5) Perform full browser SSO (interactive) and repeat call to confirm 200s resume
logs: gateway: 2026-03-11T16:12:07Z ERROR req=abc123 status=403 code=missing_role user_id=U-9843 trace=trace-0a7
auth-service: 2026-03-11T16:12:07Z WARN refresh-handler user=U-9843 refresh_okta=true roles_claim=null ttl=3599 request_id=req-xyz
okta-logs (partial): 2026-03-11T16:12:06Z Okta OIDC refresh token used for user U-9843 deviceTrust=true claims=---(redacted)---
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: claim-mapping change in auth-service dropped 'roles' when refresh token path used a different Okta token format for device-trust sessions.
Reproduced in staging with a scripted refresh loop: after N=1 refresh the auth-service returned a session token without role claims ~30% of runs.
Auth-service code path: two separate code paths handle 'interactive' vs 'refresh' OIDC responses; device-trust tokens occasionally take the 'refresh' path that omits group mapping call to SCIM cache.
Okta confirmed device-trust tokens include the groups but in a different claim name when a config flag 'use_client_claims' is set. Our mapping did not handle the alternate claim name.
Observed a backlog on SCIM delta processor around the same window (queue depth ~1200) which increased chance of stale group cache being used during refresh flow.

Short-term mitigation deployed: auth-service change to normalize both claim names and force a role-recompute on refresh if roles_claim is missing. Also added a cache eviction trigger on 403 from gateway.
Long-term: add end-to-end integration tests for Okta device-trust refresh path; increase SCIM processor concurrency; add observability for claim-variance frequency.
comments: Lina Martinez (2026-03-10): Ticket created after Pager alert from #internal-auth. Initial triage assigned to Samir.
Samir Patel (2026-03-10): Confirmed replication in staging. Added temporary cache eviction in auth-service and rolled to prod-canary. Requesting SRE to watch deploys and CI failures.
Jordan Lee, SRE (2026-03-11): Observed reduced 403s on canary. SCIM processor backlog cleared after bumping worker count from 4->8. Noted elevated DB read latency correlated with backlog window.
Okta Support (2026-03-12): Confirmed device-trust OIDC responses can emit group claims under 'groups' or 'okta_groups' depending on client config. Recommended robust mapping.
Samir Patel (2026-03-13): Deployed mapping fix and forced role recompute on refresh. Monitoring for 48h. Scheduling follow-up for permanent tests and SCIM scaling.
resolution: Mitigated: prod hotfix normalizes alternate group claim names and forces RBAC recompute on refresh; cache-eviction workaround added. Follow-up items: expand E2E tests, increase SCIM processor capacity, add metric for claim-variance frequency. Owner: Samir Patel. Planned permanent rollout window: 2026-03-18.
